PullRequest.Title: Keep SDK marketplace add progress and errors in quick input
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Stacked on #343480. Addresses the feedback that adding an SDK-owned plugin marketplace closes the input during the request and surfaces failures in a command error dialog.

- Keep Add Plugin Marketplace visible and busy while the provider adds the marketplace; disable input and prevent duplicate submissions.
- Display provider failures as inline validation, preserving the source for correction and retry. Clear the error when the user edits the source.
- Return to marketplace management after success or dismissal, preserving existing navigation. A dismissed input is not reopened or updated by a late provider result.
- Preserve the non-provider configuration path and existing source validation.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.test.ts --browser chromium` — passed, 23 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Commit hygiene — passed.

Tests cover pending progress, duplicate submission, inline errors and retry, source validation, and dismissal during pending success or failure. Live SDK/network installation was not exercised.

## Manual Test

1. Select a harness with native marketplace management and run Chat: Manage Plugin Marketplaces.
2. Choose Add Marketplace and submit a nonexistent repository.
3. Verify the input stays visible and busy, then displays an inline error with the entered source preserved instead of a modal error.
4. Correct the source and retry. Verify marketplace management returns after success.
5. Dismiss the input during a pending add. Verify a late result does not reopen the input.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed promise lifetime, loop re-entry, provider call chain, SDK RPCs, and absence of a mutation limiter are all directly traced in repository code; only the duration and how often users repeat dismissal are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Agent Host/SDK marketplace add and inventory-list RPCs, plus their retained async handlers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each time a user dismisses a slow add and re-enters Add Marketplace, another provider.add can start while every earlier add is still pending; outstanding remote operations therefore grow linearly with repeated dismiss-and-resubmit cycles.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: An avoidable burst of concurrent SDK RPC and remote marketplace work, increasing Agent Host load and request latency.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The built-in input resolved before provider.add started, and manageProviderMarketplaces awaited provider.add before returning to its loop, so one action invocation could not expose another Add Marketplace flow while an add was pending.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: onDidHide now resolves promptMarketplaceSource immediately even when its async onDidAccept listener is still awaiting addMarketplace. The caller continues the management loop, calls provider.list, and can expose another add dialog while the prior provider.add remains live.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 558 resolves the outer prompt on hide while the added async accept path at lines 575-576 can still be awaiting provider.add; this new split lifetime is what permits loop re-entry and subsequent adds before completion.
Findings.Title: Keep dismissed marketplace adds behind the in-flight operation
Findings.Impact: When an SDK marketplace registration is slow, pressing Escape and trying Add Marketplace again can overlap multiple registrations. The concrete provider forwards each add across the Agent Host boundary to the SDK and performs a follow-up marketplace-list RPC; AgentHostManagementService tracks these mutations but applies no limiter, so repeated retries can create a real concurrent RPC burst.
Findings.Evidence: The changed hide handler disposes the input and resolves at line 558 independently of the onDidAccept handler's `await addMarketplace(source)`. `manageProviderMarketplaces` immediately `continue`s and starts `provider.list`; `AgentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.add` forwards to `agentHostService.addPluginMarketplace`, and `CopilotAgent.addPluginMarketplace` performs the SDK add RPC followed by `listPluginMarketplaces`. `_runMutation` invokes operations immediately and only records them for shutdown, so it does not serialize overlapping adds.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve dismissal of the UI, but keep the action/provider mutation serialized: do not let the management loop expose another add until the in-flight add settles, or maintain an action-scoped in-flight promise/guard that the next add awaits.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful SDK-owned marketplace add while the input remains visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits provider.list before showing management, then the custom input awaits provider.add before hiding; CopilotAgent.addPluginMarketplace awaits the SDK add RPC and a refreshed inventory list before success, after which the management loop performs its next list before showing the picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forwards marketplace registration to Agent Host; CopilotAgent performs SDK marketplace add and follow-up list RPCs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One add RPC and one internal list RPC per successful submission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider.add, SDK add RPC, and follow-up list RPC occurred after the built-in input closed; the operation was awaited by the management loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both complete before the input reports success and management navigation resumes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lists provider marketplaces to build the management picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial list and one list after successful add.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial and post-success list calls occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each list must complete before its corresponding management picker appears.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source submission and the number of configured marketplaces returned for picker construction; one add is active because busy/enabled guards reject duplicate accepts in the same input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider.add at a time while the same input remains visible. The Agent Host mutation wrapper does not limit concurrency, but the per-input busy guard suffices on this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No action-level cache or coalescing is used; each management-loop iteration performs a fresh provider.list. Cold and warm behavior are therefore equivalent at this layer, with any SDK caching unknown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the busy guard, await chain, and RPC implementations are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK RPC duration and remote repository work vary by provider/source, but the serialized one-submission mechanism is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on the ordinary success path; boundary count and serialization are effectively unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provider add fails inline and the user corrects and retries
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each accepted valid source awaits provider.add before the input is re-enabled; failures are rendered inline, and a subsequent edited submission starts only after the prior attempt has settled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit valid retry; failed calls generally do not reach the success-only follow-up inventory list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One provider.add occurred after the built-in input returned; a failure ended the action instead of supporting an inline retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The input stays disabled until the attempt settles.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit user retry attempts; configured marketplace count affects synchronous duplicate validation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider.add per visible input at a time due to inputBox.busy; retries are sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Failures are not cached, intentionally permitting corrected retries. No duplicate request coalescing is needed because the busy guard suppresses repeated accepts during an attempt.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the finally block re-enables input only after each await and the busy guard blocks duplicate accepts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Retry count is user-controlled and normally small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression by itself: repeated boundary work corresponds to explicit, sequential retries needed by the new UX.

Scenarios.Scenario: User dismisses the input while an SDK marketplace add is pending, then starts another add
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new onDidHide handler resolves promptMarketplaceSource immediately, so manageProviderMarketplaces continues and awaits provider.list while the first onDidAccept handler still awaits provider.add. Once that list returns, the picker exposes Add Marketplace again without waiting for the prior add.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Leaves the current Agent Host/SDK marketplace add RPC live after UI dismissal and allows subsequent adds to start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N overlapping add RPC chains for N dismiss-and-resubmit cycles; each successful chain also performs a follow-up SDK inventory-list RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The built-in input closed before provider.add began, and the management loop awaited that add, so another add flow was not available during the operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The old add is moved off the reopened management UI's critical path, but continues consuming remote resources concurrently with newer operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Calls provider.list immediately on each post-dismissal loop re-entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fresh list per dismissal cycle, potentially concurrent with all pending adds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no post-dismissal loop re-entry while provider.add was pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The list gates reopening the management picker but does not gate on pending adds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of dismiss-and-resubmit cycles while slow adds remain pending; effective cardinality is one additional add operation and management-list call per cycle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to N provider.add/SDK RPC chains can overlap after N cycles. AgentHostManagementService._runMutation starts each operation immediately and only tracks it for shutdown, providing no limiter or sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no in-flight add registry, coalescing, or action-level guard. Each loop re-entry performs a fresh list, and each resubmission starts a distinct add.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high; the split promise lifetime, immediate loop continue, RPC call chain, and lack of limiter are directly proven.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often users dismiss and retry, and the SDK's per-add remote cost, are uncertain; slow/error-prone repositories make the trigger realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity concurrency burst; one finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local/non-provider marketplace configuration and invalid provider input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The local path still uses quickInputService.input and writes configuration only after valid input. On the provider path, invalid or duplicate input is rejected synchronously before provider.add.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: No direct filesystem operation is added by this diff; the existing configuration service update persists one settings change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One update for a valid local submission; zero for invalid input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical local path and configuration update behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing update is awaited before the local action returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured marketplace count used for parse and duplicate scan per submission; typically a small user-managed list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No provider mutation for invalid input; local configuration update is a single awaited operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configured sources are snapshotted once per prompt. No cache behavior changed on the local path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the addMarketplace callback is only passed for provider management and validation precedes invocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configured-source list sizes vary but are bounded by user configuration and expected to be small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the non-provider path is preserved and invalid submissions do not cross the provider boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the full two-file diff and traced provider add/list calls through the Agent Host and SDK RPC layers. Normal success and inline retry remain serialized, but dismissing a pending custom input resolves the outer flow while its add remains live, allowing repeated user actions to create overlapping provider mutations. Submitted one medium-severity concurrency-burst finding.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
